snapshots.description: The Happy Ending problem, n = 7. Erdős and Szekeres proved that every large enough set of points in general position contains a convex polygon with n vertices, and conjectured that 2^(n-2) + 1 points always suffice. It's known up to hexagons (17 points, by computer in 2006). This project goes for heptagons: every 33 points in general position contain a convex heptagon. The plan: encode it as a SAT problem, break its symmetries, prove it unsatisfiable, and check the proof independently. Meanwhile, a hunt for 32 points with no convex heptagon, which would show 33 is the best possible.

snapshots.description: The Happy Ending problem, n = 7. Erdős and Szekeres proved that every large enough set of points in general position contains a convex polygon with n vertices, and conjectured that 2^(n-2) + 1 points always suffice. It's known up to hexagons (17 points, by computer in 2006). This project goes for heptagons: every 33 points in general position contain a convex heptagon. The plan: encode it as a SAT problem, break its symmetries, prove it unsatisfiable, and check the proof independently. Meanwhile, a hunt for 32 points with no convex heptagon, which would show 33 is the best possible.
